name: The Möbius Strip Club
subtitle: One surface. One edge. No way to be inside it wrongly.
description:
The frontage is red and the light coming off it is not, quite. Inside, the room is a room, and the corridor off the room is a corridor, and if you follow the corridor in one direction with no turns and no doors you will arrive at the room, facing the way you set off, having never once reversed. Patrons do this on purpose. It is considered a thing to do while drunk, the way other towns have a hill.

The stage does its impossible business: dancers continuously undressing, and never at any point undressed, an act that resolves the moment you stop watching and refuses to while you do. The bar is long and the menu is a provocation. And at the edges — behind the booths, along the corridor where the light gives out — the walls occasionally stop being opaque, and what is on the other side of them is not the street.
revisit:
The Insta-gators register your entry the way a spreadsheet registers a row: without interest, without objection, and without any evidence afterwards that the row was ever added. One of them is not there and then the sentence you are standing in acquires a second clause and it is, nine feet of tailored patience with a jaw in it, circling back on your presence in this space.

Ginny is at the till with gin in her hand and none of it in her voice. The far wall goes to glass at some point in the next few minutes, for two seconds, as it does nine times a night. Ninety people are on this floor and not one of them is standing in front of it.

lucid.2: The music has gaps in it. Not silences — gaps, of a length that a person would take to change a line.
lucid.3: In the third gap, before the music resumes, there is a sound in the room that is not in the room: keys, four of them, struck hard and close together, and then a carriage going back.
lucid.4: The gaps are not gaps in the music. The music is what is filling the gaps, and it is being put there afterwards, over the top of a room that has no sound of its own.

ambient: A patron walks the corridor for a joke, comes back grinning from the wrong direction, and cannot be talked out of the grin or into an explanation.
The barman pours something into a glass that is already holding it, and the level does not rise, and he does not appear to expect it to.
Somewhere behind the booths a wall goes briefly to glass, shows a stretch of black stone and a green lamp and the corner of a desk, and comes back. Two seconds. Nobody at the near tables turns round.
The music changes and ninety people change weight at the same moment without any of them deciding to, and the room resettles half a step to the left of where it was.
An Insta-gator apologises to somebody for something that has not happened, courteously, and offers to circle back on it.

objects.name: the main sign
objects.description:
THE MÖBIUS STRIP CLUB, in a red that has been chosen by somebody with an entire opinion about red — not the red of a bar sign, which is chosen from a catalogue, but a specific and slightly unfashionable crimson that somebody paid extra to have bent into tube.

The umlaut is a nice touch and is doing no phonetic work whatsoever. Nobody in this parish says it, nobody has ever said it, and it makes no difference to the vowel. It is there to be looked at, which in this town is a perfectly legitimate job for a piece of punctuation to hold down.

The letters are steady. They have been steady every single time you have come here, in a parish where the neon at Mary's has four settings and cycles through all of them, and where the sign over your own building cannot hold on to its final letter.

This one does not move. Somebody is holding it still.
objects.repeat: Steady. Red. A joke about surfaces, told once, at some expense, in neon, by somebody who could afford to have it made and never needed it explained.
objects.monocle:
Through the gold the letters detach from the board and reassemble, unhurried, with the deliberation of a man rearranging a hand of cards, and settle into:

REVILO'S TRAP BUILT

They hold for as long as you keep the lens up. Then they go back, one letter at a time, in the reverse of the order they came.

passive.text: A Möbius strip is the one surface with no inside. That is not a name for a club. That is a disclosure, hung over the door in red, where nobody has to read it.

check.prompt: Do the letters properly. Not the impression of the trick — the arithmetic of it. Count what THE MÖBIUS STRIP CLUB actually contains, and count what it gave you.
check.success:
You count. You count twice, because the first count is the one where a man finds what he expected.

THE MÖBIUS STRIP CLUB has no A in it. It has no V. REVILO'S TRAP BUILT has both, and has them prominently, and REVILO is where they live.

This is not an anagram. An anagram would be a coincidence with good manners. This is a rearrangement that has *brought letters with it* — which means the sign did not reveal a hidden name. Somebody spelled a name at you, and used the sign as a surface to do it on, and did not check whether the surface could afford the letters.

Whoever did it wanted to be read more than they wanted to be plausible.
check.failure:
The letters swim. Not the neon — the neon is steady, the neon has been steady all fortnight — the *letters*, in the reading of them.

You get as far as counting the Bs, lose the count to the music, start again, and lose it again to the specific and unwelcome fact that the music stopped for exactly as long as it took you to lose it, and started again on the beat you would have finished on.

clue.title: The sign spent letters it did not have
clue.text: REVILO'S TRAP BUILT contains an A and a V. THE MÖBIUS STRIP CLUB contains neither. This is not a hidden name surfacing — it is a name being spelled at you by something that did not check the supply.

clue.title: REVILO'S TRAP BUILT
clue.text: Under the monocle the club's sign rearranges itself into REVILO'S TRAP BUILT, holds while the lens is up, and reassembles in reverse when it comes down.

objects.name: the corridor with no turns
objects.description:
It leaves the main room at the left of the stage and it does not turn.

There is no point along it at which it turns. You have walked it slowly, twice, paying the specific kind of attention that a man pays when he intends to be able to swear to something afterwards, with a hand on the wall the entire way — and it does not turn, and it does not curve, and there is no shallow bend disguised by the lighting.

And it delivers you back into the main room at the *right* of the stage, facing forward, on the same side of the room you started on.

The wall on the outside of the walk is papered in a heavy green flock. The wall on the inside of the walk is papered in the same green flock, from the same roll, matched at the pattern.

There is no inside of the walk. That is what a Möbius strip is for, and somebody has built one out of flock wallpaper and put a bar in it and applied for a licence.
objects.repeat: The second walk is shorter. Not because the corridor is shorter but because you are, on the second walk, a man who has already done it once — and that turns out to be a property the corridor takes into account.
objects.monocle: Through the gold the corridor is straight and short — nine feet, a dead end, a wall. The loop is not in the architecture. The loop is in the account of the architecture: the same nine feet, described four times, with the fourth description ending where the first began.

passive.text: A Möbius strip has one surface and one edge. If this corridor is genuinely one, then there is no outside of it, and everyone who has ever walked it — including you, twice — is on the same side of the paper as everyone else. That is not a comforting property of this building. That is the least comforting property of this building.
Your legs kept a count even when you did not. Twenty-two paces out, and you arrive back after twenty-two, and a loop that returns you in the distance it took to leave is not a loop. It is a fold.

clue.title: Not a loop — a fold
clue.text: Twenty-two paces out, twenty-two paces back to the start, in a corridor with no turns. Under the monocle it is nine feet and a dead end, described four times.

check.prompt: Walk the corridor with no turns all the way round, at a steady pace, without putting a hand on the wall.
check.success:
The floor is off-level the whole way and the off-level rotates, slowly, so that down is always about four degrees ahead of you. You walk it the way you walk a deck.

You arrive facing the way you set off, having never reversed, and — because you kept your feet and therefore your count — with the knowledge that the corridor is eleven paces longer coming back than it was going out, and that you only went one way.
check.failure: Four degrees of wrong, continuously, and about two-thirds of the way round the wall gets a hand whether you offer it or not, and the count goes, and you come out grinning like the patrons do and knowing exactly as much as they do.

clue.title: Eleven paces longer, one way
clue.text: Walked properly, the Möbius corridor is eleven paces longer on the return than the outward leg — and there is only one leg.

objects.name: the wall behind the far booth
objects.description:
The booths at the back are where the light stops trying. The last one is upholstered in a red that has gone the colour of an old argument, and the leather is cracked along the top edge, and the wall behind it does the thing.

It does it for about two seconds at a stretch. It does not do it on request, it does not do it more often for an attentive observer, and it does it roughly nine times a night at intervals that are not regular.

The wall stops being a wall. Not fading, not shimmering, not going gradually — simply *not being the item that was there*, in the way a word stops being on a page when it has been struck out.

And behind it is somewhere else. Twice it has been a stretch of obsidian and a row of vault doors with brass plates on them. Once it was a low room with a green-shaded lamp and a desk under it, and paper drifted across the desk, and a chair pulled out and left pulled out, and nobody in the chair.
objects.repeat: It does it again while you are sitting down, which it has now done four times in your presence, and the interval between them is not regular and the duration is regular to the fraction of a second.

lucid.3: The chair is not pulled out. The chair is pushed back, which is a different event with a different cause, and the cause of a chair being pushed back is somebody standing up in a hurry.

objects.monocle: The gold holds it open. The wall does not come back for as long as the lens is up, and the room behind it is fully furnished and entirely ordinary and has a waste basket beside the desk with paper in it, and the paper has been screwed up by a hand that was not pleased.

passive.text: Two seconds is not a glitch. Two seconds is a duration somebody chose — long enough that a patron sees it, short enough that a patron does not get to check.

The chair. Somebody was sitting in it and is not now, and left in the middle of something, and has not come back to push the chair in — and a person who does not push their chair in is a person who intends to be back within the minute.

check.prompt: Get to it while it is open. Two seconds, nine feet, and nine feet of alligator between you and it who have been waiting all evening for somebody to try exactly this.
check.success:
You go on the second the wall opens, and not a beat after — which is the difference between the attempt working and the attempt being a story the Insta-gators tell.

Your hand goes through where the wall is. There is no cold, no membrane, no resistance and no drama. On the far side, the air is warmer and smells of dust on a hot bulb, and your fingers close on the thing nearest the edge, and then a hand of considerable professionalism closes on your collar and the wall is a wall again and you are sitting down, and you were always sitting down, and nobody has moved.

In your fist: a ball of paper, screwed up hard. Smoothed out, it is a page. Most of it is struck through. What survives the strike-through is a single line: *and Onions, who by this point had stopped being able to tell the difference, went to the club.*
check.failure:
You go a quarter-second after the wall opens, and a full second after the room has registered that you are going to.

You do not reach the wall. What you reach is nine feet of tailored patience that has, at some point in the interval, come to be standing between you and it, and which catches you the way a door catches a draught — without effort, without malice, and with a small professional noise of a box being ticked.

clue.title: A page, mostly struck out
clue.text: Retrieved through the open wall: a screwed-up page, almost entirely struck through. The surviving line reads: 'and Onions, who by this point had stopped being able to tell the difference, went to the club.'

item.name: a page, mostly struck out
item.description: One surviving line, about a man who had stopped being able to tell the difference. It is in the past tense, which is the part you keep going back to.

clue.title: They were already there
clue.text: The Insta-gator that stopped you was between you and the wall before you moved. Not faster than you — earlier than you.

objects.name: the drinks menu
objects.description:
Letterpressed on good card, deckle-edged, because the club has standards about the surfaces on which it tells you things.

WRITER'S BLOCK — gin, bitter, nothing else, served without ice and without apology.
RECURRING DREAM — as above, again.
THE UNRELIABLE NARRATOR — ask, and be told something.
SECOND PERSON — the house special. You drink it. You have always been going to drink it.

The first three are cocktail names of the sort that a club with this much red in it is entitled to. They are jokes about writing, told by somebody who knows enough about writing for the jokes to land, in a building that ninety people a night walk through without reading the card.

The last one is not a cocktail name.

The last one is a grammatical case. Somebody has put a grammatical case on a drinks menu, given it a description in the second person about drinking it, and left the price blank — and the blank is *printed*, with a rule under it the same length as the other four.
objects.repeat: SECOND PERSON is still unpriced. The blank has been printed rather than left — there is a rule under it where a price would go, and the rule is the same length as the rules under the other four.
objects.monocle: The gold does not change the card. It changes the hand that set it: the letterpress impressions are too deep and too even, and every one of them has been struck the same number of times, and the number is the number of times a key is struck by somebody who is not confident.

passive.text: Gin, bitter, no ice, no apology. That is not a cocktail, that is a diagnosis, and you would like two.

Four drinks. Writer's block, recurrence, unreliability, and the second person. That is not a bar list. That is a set of problems, in the order a person encounters them, and somebody has been drinking their way down it.

check.prompt: Order the Writer's Block. It is gin and bitter and no ice, it will cost you your Logic for the evening, and there has never been a moment in your life when that was a worse trade than it is now.
check.success:
Gin, bitter, no ice, no apology. It goes down like a decision.

And the room loosens — not blurs, loosens, the way a paragraph loosens when a man stops trying to make it behave. The impossible corridor stops being an outrage and becomes a feature. The dancers' paradox resolves itself into simple good manners. Everything in Silvora Reefs that has been braced against your attention puts its shoulders down, and for the length of one drink you and the town are on the same side of the paper, and it is, unforgivably, pleasant.
check.failure:
Gin, bitter, no ice, no apology, and it arrives in a glass that was already holding it, which you watch happen and then drink anyway.

It does not loosen anything. It goes down and sits there and adds its own opinion to a night that had enough. The barman says 'Same again?' before the glass is down, and he is not being attentive, he is being early.

objects.name: a laminated card by the service door
objects.description:
Screwed to the wall at alligator eye level, which is to say at a height that makes a standing man stoop and look ridiculous doing it.

SECURITY ALIGNMENT — PATRON ANOMALY AWARENESS
1. Identify the anomaly the patron has surfaced.
2. Do not confirm. Do not deny. Redirect.
3. If redirect fails, reposition the patron.
4. If reposition fails, escalate to the Coalition.
5. Post-incident: the anomaly did not occur. Log the anomaly.

The fifth line has been laminated over a previous fifth line. Held to the light, the old one shows through, and the old one said: *Post-incident: the anomaly did not occur.* Somebody has added the second sentence since.
objects.repeat: You stoop and read it again. Line five is still two sentences where it used to be one, and the second sentence is still in a slightly different face from the other four, and the lamination has not been broken.

passive.text: 'The anomaly did not occur' and 'log the anomaly' cannot both be instructions to the same person about the same event. Unless the log is not a record. Unless the log is the thing that makes it not have occurred.

Line two is the whole doctrine. Do not confirm, do not deny — because confirming makes it real and denying makes it discussable. Redirect is the only move that leaves the anomaly unspoken, and unspoken is the state they are actually protecting.

clue.title: Do not confirm. Do not deny. Redirect.
clue.text: Insta-gator security doctrine: surface, redirect, reposition, escalate to the Coalition. Final line, amended later: 'the anomaly did not occur. Log the anomaly.'

check.prompt: A laminated card by the service door, in the language institutions use on each other. Requisition it.
check.success:
You take it off the hook the way a man takes a thing he is entitled to take, and nobody stops you, because nobody in a service corridor has ever stopped a man who took something off a hook without hesitating.

It is a procedure card. Step four is 'Log the anomaly.' Step five is 'The anomaly did not occur.' Both steps are printed. Neither is a correction of the other.
check.failure: You reach for it and the reach turns into a gesture at it, and the gesture turns into a question, and the question is answered by an alligator in a suit who is *terribly* sorry but the card is not for patrons, and holds the door for you with real regret.

clue.title: Log the anomaly. It did not occur.
clue.text: The Möbius procedure card prints 'Log the anomaly' and 'The anomaly did not occur' as consecutive steps, neither correcting the other.

objects.name: the stage
objects.description:
The act is the club's whole reputation and it is, technically, one gesture performed continuously: the dancers are undressing, and are always undressing, and at no point in any evening in the recorded history of this establishment has any of them been undressed.

It is not a tease. A tease has a destination it is withholding. This has no destination — it is the present continuous, held, indefinitely, by four people who are extremely good at it and show no signs of strain.

The patrons accept this. Not tolerate — *accept*, in the round-eyed, faintly reverent way of a congregation who came for one thing and stayed for another. Nobody in here watches it as an erotic proposition; you can see that in the faces, which are wrong for it.

They watch it the way people watch a fire, or a tide coming in: something that is plainly going somewhere and is never going to arrive, and is restful precisely and entirely because of it.
objects.repeat: Still going. Still not arrived. The restfulness of it is the part that takes getting used to — an act with no resolution should be unbearable, and instead the whole room is comfortable, and the comfort is doing something.
objects.monocle: Through the gold there is nobody on the stage. There is a sentence on the stage, and the sentence is *she was still undressing*, and it has been left in the present continuous by somebody who could not decide how it ended and went to get a drink instead.

passive.text: Look at the faces of the dancers rather than the act. They are not performing. They are waiting — with the particular patience of somebody halfway through a sentence, holding the pose, until whoever is writing them comes back.

clue.title: Left in the present continuous
clue.text: Through the monocle the stage holds no dancers, only the sentence 'she was still undressing', abandoned mid-tense by somebody who went to get a drink.

check.prompt: The act resolves the instant you stop watching and refuses to while you do. Catch it in the gap.
check.success:
You look away, and back, faster than the deciding part of you can be consulted — and for about a third of a second the stage is *between states*, which is not a thing a stage can be.

What is on it in that third of a second is not dancers. It is a stage direction, unperformed, waiting to be given a body, and it notices being seen and gets dressed extremely quickly.
check.failure: Away, and back. The act is exactly as it was, continuous, impeccable, and entirely unbothered, and the room's opinion of a man snapping his head about at a strip club is available to you without anybody having to voice it.

clue.title: A stage direction, unperformed
clue.text: Caught in the gap, the Möbius stage holds an unperformed direction rather than dancers, and dresses itself the moment it is seen.

objects.name: the wall, no longer closing
objects.description:
It went transparent at the usual time and it has not come back.

Two seconds became four. Four became eleven. Eleven became the rest of the evening, and it is still going, and the black stone and the green lamp and the corner of a desk are all simply there now, at the back of a strip club, behind the last booth, in full view of ninety people.

The Insta-gators have stopped repositioning anybody. That is the detail that tells you where the evening has got to: there is no longer a coherent account of this room for them to protect, and line two of the card requires an account to redirect people toward, and there isn't one.

The music is still playing. Nobody is dancing.

One of them is standing beside you, watching it with you, nine feet of tailored patience with its hands folded, not doing anything at all. After a while it says — quietly, without the register, entirely off script — "Yeah. That's it, then."
objects.monocle: Through the gold the club is nine feet of corridor and a dead end, and always was, and the dead end is standing open.
objects.repeat: Still open. It is not going to close on its own, and that is not the same thing as it being patient, and you have stood in front of this one on three separate evenings now.

passive.text: Every deduction you have made for a fortnight terminates here. There is nothing further to work out. The next thing is not a conclusion, it is a step.
Four inches of nothing, and a floor on the other side that will take a man's weight. The body has already decided. It has been leaning that way since the harbour.

check.prompt:
Go through. Nothing is stopping you and nothing has been stopping you for some time, and that is the part that will need thinking about afterwards, on the other side, if there is an afterwards and if there is a side.

There is no way back through a seam. Whatever is unfinished in Silvora Reefs stays unfinished.
check.success:
You go through.

There is no membrane and no cold and no drama, and the last thing behind you is somebody not saying anything, and then you are standing on boards in a room nine feet by eleven with a green-shaded lamp in it.
check.failure:
Your foot goes over the edge and your weight does not follow it, and you stand for a while in a doorway with one leg committed, which is not a dignified way to arrive anywhere and is a completely honest description of the last fortnight.

Then the knee that has been going since the harbour makes the decision for you, and you go through badly, and land on boards, in a room nine feet by eleven, with a green-shaded lamp in it.

objects.name: the angles of the room
objects.description:
Stand at the corner by the service door and sight along the near wall to the far one, and they are not parallel. Close one eye, take it properly, use the brass rail as a straight edge: not parallel, by a margin small enough to argue about and large enough to see.

Now walk to the other corner and do the same. Still not parallel — and not parallel by a different amount, in the other direction, which is not a thing a room is able to be.

The club does not appear to notice. Drinks are poured level and stay level. The stage is level. Eleven staff walk this floor nightly at speed, carrying trays, in low light, and not one of them has ever put a foot wrong on it or remarked that the room is a difficult shape.

They have adjusted. Everyone in here has adjusted, continuously, without ever being told there was anything to adjust to, and they have been doing it so long and so well that the adjustment has stopped being visible even to the people performing it.
objects.repeat: Sight it again. The error has moved. It is always small, it is always somewhere, and it is never twice in the same corner — and tonight the near wall is the one that is out.
objects.monocle: Through the gold the walls are ruled lines and the ruling is freehand, and every few feet there is a place where the line has been gone over a second time to straighten it, and the second pass is always slightly better than the first.

clue.title: Not parallel, and not consistently so
clue.text: The Möbius's walls are out of true, by a different amount and in a different direction depending on where you sight from. The staff walk it nightly without difficulty.

check.prompt: Take the angles properly. Two sightlines, a fixed point, and the discipline not to blink at the wrong moment.
check.success:
Fix on the brass rail, sight the far corner, hold it, and take the angle again from the same spot forty seconds later.

It has changed. It has changed by a quantity too small to see and large enough to measure against a rail, and it has changed in the direction of *true*.

That is the whole finding and it is worth the crick in the neck: the room is not drifting out of square. It is being brought into it, a fraction at a time, between the moments anybody is looking — and the corrections are not random, they are cumulative, and they are the work of somebody going back over a line that did not come out right the first time.
check.failure: You take the angle, and take it again, and the second one disagrees with the first by about the amount a man's own neck disagrees with itself at eleven at night in a room with this much noise in it. Nothing here will hold still long enough to be accused.

clue.title: Corrected, a fraction at a time
clue.text: Measured twice against a fixed rail forty seconds apart, the Möbius's walls move — toward true, cumulatively, between glances. The room is not drifting. It is being gone back over.

objects.name: the floor, and everybody on it
objects.description:
Nobody comes in the front. Ginny said so on the first night and she was not making conversation — they arrive by the side, by the corridor, by the stair that does not go anywhere it ought to, and the front door stands open all evening onto a street that ninety people have declined to use.

Once they are in, they distribute themselves across the room with a great deal of care.

It does not look like care. It looks like a busy floor on a good night: knots by the bar, a press at the stage end, couples working the edges. But watch it long enough and a shape resolves out of it, and the shape has a hole in it. There are eleven staff and about ninety patrons and not one of them is standing in the eight or so square feet directly in front of the far booth.

The carpet there is newer than the carpet anywhere else, because nothing has walked on it.
objects.repeat: The floor has rearranged itself since you looked and the far booth still has nobody in front of it, and the eight square feet of clear carpet has not changed shape, only position.
objects.monocle:
Through the gold the floor has a shape drawn on it in a dotted line — eight square feet, roughly oval, in front of the far booth.

Everybody is outside the dotted line. Not near it, not respecting it: *outside* it, the way people stand outside a thing that has been marked.

And the dotted line has been there longer than the carpet. It is under the carpet. It was drawn on the boards, and then a carpet was laid over it, and ninety people a night have gone on standing outside a line that nobody alive in this building has ever seen.

clue.title: Nobody stands in front of the far booth
clue.text: Ninety patrons and eleven staff distribute themselves across the Möbius floor with care, and not one of them stands where the far booth can see them.

check.prompt: Ninety people are avoiding the same eight square feet and none of them is thinking about it. Ask the room why.
check.success:
It comes up all at once, the way a room's mind does, and it is not a thought any individual in here is having.

They are not avoiding the booth. They are *leaving it clear* — and the difference is the difference between a man stepping round a puddle and a man stepping round a place where somebody fell over once.

None of them knows why. Ask any one of them and they will give you a reason about the draught or the speakers and the reason will be sincere. But the shape they are keeping is a courtesy shape, and this parish has been keeping it, nightly, without instruction, for longer than the carpet — and somewhere underneath it is the knowledge that the wall behind that booth is a window, and that it is polite not to stand in front of a window when somebody is looking out of it.
check.failure:
Ninety people having a night out, loudly, in a building shaped like an argument.

Whatever the room knows collectively, it is not in a mood to be asked about it by a man standing at the edge of the floor with his coat still on and his weight on the back foot — and the room is entitled to that, and the room has ninety perfectly good reasons to be enjoying itself instead.

clue.title: They are leaving it clear
clue.text: The Möbius floor keeps a gap in front of the far booth — not avoidance but courtesy, kept nightly without instruction for longer than the carpet, by people who each have a sincere and different explanation for it.

exits.hang_hi: the harbour road home, which has never once been the same length twice
exits.durry_kwain: up the hill, toward vanilla and an apology for a wait
exits.rest_assured: the climb to the obsidian, which from here is somehow downhill
exits.outside_inn: further along the harbour road, to a door with weather behind it
exits.gs_spot: up and inward, to mirrors that do not agree
